paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God decides how He is worshiped, and we don't get to make it up as we go. Moses says that right now, "everyone does what seems right in his own eyes" (Deuteronomy 12:8). Then he tells Israel to go to the place the LORD will choose, "a dwelling for His Name" (Deuteronomy 12:5). Worship isn't a recipe you improvise, and I know, because I tried that once and the smoke alarm sang for me all night.

Now look at what God's way gives them. They get to come before the LORD with their households and rejoice, because "the LORD your God has blessed you" (Deuteronomy 12:7). The Levite gets an invitation too, and Moses says to be careful not to neglect the Levites (Deuteronomy 12:19). The LORD's way is no gloomy rulebook. It's a table, and everybody has a seat at it.

So Moses ends with a warning, and it's for us too. Don't go asking how the nations served their gods and then say you'll do likewise (Deuteronomy 12:30). "See that you do everything I command you; do not add to it or subtract from it" (Deuteronomy 12:32). Baker, God's Word is complete as He gave it, so trust it, keep it, and don't go borrowing a recipe from somebody else's kitchen.
